# Certifier conformance statement

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit.
     Source: documentation/compliance/certifiers/<certifier>/forms/*.yaml
     Regenerate: cd trazo-back && poetry run python manage.py certifier_conformance -->

How Trazo lines up against each certifying agent's own Organic System Plan forms, question by question. Registered: CCOF, OTCO, WSDA.
Generated from the conformance register, which is checked against the shipped OSP module
registry by `certifications/tests/test_certifier_conformance_register.py` — a question that is
renamed, removed or added without a decision fails that test rather than quietly making
this document wrong.

Statuses: **Covered** — the fact is capturable and reaches an artifact a certifier reads.
**Partial** — captured but incomplete. **Not covered** — no home in the product today.
**Out of scope** — deliberately not built, with the reason stated.

Severity is about what a reviewer at that certifier does with it: **P0** the packet is bounced or
asserts something untrue · **P1** a request for information · **P2** noticed, tolerated ·
**P3** cosmetic.

## Where we stand

### C2 Crops Acreage & Land History

*C2 · rev. 2024/06/05 · retrieved 2026-09-09*  
<https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

**When OTCO requires it:** C1 Crop Activities Checklist: "I/We grow crops → C2: Land History (one C2 document for each non-adjacent parcel)". C2's own header: "This form must be submitted with a new application or to add acreage, but does not need to be updated. Future crop updates may be submitted to Oregon Tilth in any written format or by phone… For updates to currently certified acreage, use FACT-04 Field, Acreage, Crop Table." So C2 is filed ONCE per parcel (at application, or when acreage is added); the annual parcel × acreage × status × crops statement is FACT-04.

Submitted with a new application or to add acreage; it does not need to be updated — future crop updates in any written format, and FACT-04 for updates to currently certified acreage. <https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

The form's own instruction: "Complete this form for all acreage to be included under certification."

The fact is captured, but only per logged event: `PestManagementEvent.pest_species` names the organism observed on each scouting or control record and prints in the audit dossier. There is no plan-level statement, so an operation whose records are thin — a first-year pilot, or a season with no pest events yet — shows nothing, and even a well-logged one gives the reviewer a column of observations to deduplicate rather than the list OTCO asks for. **Fix:** Add `pests_diseases_of_concern` [textarea] on page A, ahead of `prevention_practices`, cite § 205.206; suggest the distinct `pest_species` values from logged Pest-Management events as a prefill the operator confirms (suggest→confirm — the plan is the producer's statement under § 205.201(a), not a reading of the log); compile "Pests and diseases of concern: {answer}." |

OTCO asks for the verification METHOD and what it covers: a yes/no plus a frequency says nothing about what is tested for (prohibited substances versus pathogens), by whom, or against what threshold, and an operation that verifies by the nature of the source rather than by sampling — a municipal supply with the utility's own reports, a deep well with a one-time baseline — has no way to say so and reads as "not tested". **Fix:** Add `water_verification_method` [checkbox_group] {lab_testing, municipal_utility_reports, district_statement, source_assessment, other} with an `other` text, and `water_contaminants_tested` [checkbox_group] {prohibited_substances, pathogens, heavy_metals, other}, visible when the operation irrigates; cite § 205.202(c) / § 205.200. |

It lists every material on the plan or in the records except one marked no longer used, and one whose WSDA approval the operator recorded dated within the twelve months before the sheet; an undated approval cannot be placed in the previous year, so the material is listed. CORRECTION (live read, 2026-11-04): the paragraph below reads WSDA's Brand Name Material List as if a product on it could be skipped. It cannot: that list is a manufacturers' registry ("Certified farms and businesses should check with their certifier to update their organic system plan prior to use of any new material"), and the skip applies to materials WSDA approved for THIS operation. Earlier text: nothing on the registry row recorded whether a material was planned, in use, or already approved from a prior year, so Trazo could not answer WSDA's own framing, 'list what is NEW', at all. The module shows the same undifferentiated full list every year, which is a heavier ask than WSDA's form requires and gives a renewing operator no way to see what they can skip. Separately, the operator cannot see which listed materials are already on WSDA's own Brand Name Materials List: Trazo already syncs WSDA's own published Organic Brand Name Materials List (`WSDAMaterial`) and resolves every registry material against it alongside OMRI and the National List, printing a distinct 'WSDA' heading in the module PDF — so a WSDA-sourced match is not a generic co-equal cross-reference the way it is for a CCOF filing; it is citing WSDA's OWN list back to WSDA, which is a materially stronger fact for THIS form specifically (an operator listing an already-WSDA-listed product is exactly the case AGR 2196's own header says can be skipped for renewing operations). The module never surfaces that distinction to the OPERATOR while they are preparing this form, though: there is no view that separates 'already on the WSDA list' from 'OMRI-only or National-List-only' (materials WSDA has not independently reviewed, and cannot be assumed pre-cleared from an OMRI or National List match alone, per the WSDAMaterial model's own note that the two programs review independently). |

| Table (company name) | Company name as listed on the input label or responsible for input registration. | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.manufacturer` · `certifications.OMRIProduct.manufacturer` · `certifications.services.plan_materials.PlanMaterial.display` | Closed 2026-09-09 (fix/parcel-page-land-history, materials cut): the certifier-facing line (`PlanMaterial.display(stated_absences=True)`, used by the module PDF and the plan snapshot) states a missing cell as missing — 'manufacturer not stated', 'reason for use not stated', and for a bare National List substance 'brand and formulation not stated' — instead of omitting it, so a row that needs the cell no longer reads like a row that never did. The Materials List workbook already counts each blank per row (`fix_hint="materials_list"`) and the editor names where it is answered. Remaining, as CCOF A (manufacturer): nothing requires the column before submission; the create path takes the name alone by design. **Fix:** Completion gate on `manufacturer` for rows marked in use, per the CCOF fix. |
| Table (intended purpose) | Intended purpose of the material (fertilizer, sanitizer, etc.). | Covered | — | `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.category` | Closed 2026-11-04 (feat/wsda-2196-draft): the AGR 2196 sheet prints the operator's section on the materials list as the form's purpose word (fertilizer or soil amendment, pest, disease or weed control, production aid, post-harvest sanitizer), for every material listed, logged or not; with no section, the reason the records imply. History: unlike CCOF's own 'reason for use' column — which wants a SPECIFIC reason ('zinc deficiency') and is `not_covered` because Trazo has no such field — WSDA's own ask is a broad category word ('fertilizer', 'sanitizer'), which is exactly what the workbook's `_material_reason()` already derives from the logged event category. The gap here is narrower: that derivation only runs for event-derived workbook rows, never for the registry-derived list the module panel and PDF show, and a category word is never printed for a material the operator listed but has not yet logged an application of. |
| Table (how restrictions are met) | How you ensure this material meets any organic restrictions or requirements (e.g., soil tests are maintained to demonstrate deficiency, followed by a potable water rinse, etc.). | Covered | — | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `g3_0_seeds.treatment_verification` · `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_documentation` · `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_upload` · `certifications.PlanMaterialRestrictionStatement.how_met` · `certifications.services.material_restrictions.operator_how_met` · `certifications.services.national_list_citations.ANNOTATIONS` | Re-read 2026-11-05 (restricted-materials slice) against the shipped code: the register said "no field exists ... for a per-material compliance-verification narrative", which stopped being true with back #99 (T18, migration 0049). `PlanMaterialRestrictionStatement` holds, per material on the plan and per restriction, the operator's attributed and dated "how it is met"; the Materials Application's restrictions panel captures it, and the AGR 2196 sheet prints it in this column through `operator_how_met` (current statements only, the operator's words and nothing Trazo wrote; guard `test_wsda_agr_2196`). The regulation wording a statement answers to is offered for the § 205.602 conditions and, since migration 0071, for the § 205.601 rows whose annotation Trazo holds verbatim (fixed coppers, copper sulfate, magnesium sulfate, micronutrients), so the restricted mineral this row was P1 about can now carry the rule's own words and the operator's answer. A material with no statement prints blank and is counted as the operator's to answer, never filled. |

Its gap is carried by 'Instructions (complete list)'. |

### OFPP Organic Fraud Prevention Plan

*OFPP · rev 2025/08/27 · retrieved 2026-09-09*  
<https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

**When OTCO requires it:** C1 Crop Activities Checklist — "I/We are applying for Oregon Tilth organic certification for crop production" routes to "O1: Operation Information (required)" and "OFPP: Organic Fraud Prevention Plan". The form itself carries a not-applicable stop for perennial or wild-crop growers who buy no certified organic seed or planting stock (row 1-3).

**17 questions** — Covered 3 · Partial 10 · Not covered 4 · not questions: Instruction (asks nothing) 1

| Ref | What OTCO asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-1 | Section 1. ORGANIC FRAUD PREVENTION TEAM — identify the person or people responsible for approving, implementing, training staff, and monitoring the Organic Fraud Prevention Plan. Table: Name · Job Title/Role · Contact Info (Phone/Email). | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_accuracy_process` · `company.Establishment.ofpp_responsible_person` | FRESH — neither CCOF G8.0 §D nor WSDA §P asks for a named team, so no verdict existed to reuse. Trazo holds ONE responsible name on the Establishment (`ofpp_responsible_person`: no title, no contact, dossier-only) and a prose answer in G2.0 §C that names who keeps the plan accurate. There is no table of name · role · contact, and the four responsibilities OTCO distinguishes — approve, implement, train, monitor — cannot be assigned to different people. **Fix:** Add a repeatable `ofpp_team` field {name, role, responsibilities (approve / implement / train / monitor), contact} to G2.0 page C, seeded from `ofpp_responsible_person` for the operator to confirm, printing as OTCO's table. |
| 1-2 | How will you report possible organic fraud? Check all that apply: report to your Oregon Tilth Client Services Team · report to the supplier's certifying agent · report to the USDA National Organic Program · report to the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) State Organic Program, for CA operations · other (describe). | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_practices` · `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_other` | Reused from WSDA §P 6 (P2). `report_suspected` is one tick — "Report suspected fraud to our certifier or the NOP" — with no breakdown. WSDA wanted the TRIGGERS for a report; OTCO wants the CHANNELS (own certifier, the supplier's certifier, the NOP, CDFA). A certifier cannot tell from the tick whether a California operation knows CDFA is a reporting route, or whether the operation would report upstream to a supplier's agent. **Fix:** Add `fraud_reporting_channels` checkbox_group {own_certifier, suppliers_certifier, usda_nop, cdfa_sop, other} shown when `report_suspected` is selected — beside the `fraud_reporting_triggers` group WSDA §P 6 proposes. |
| 1-3 | If you grow perennial crops or harvest wild crops, do you buy certified organic products like seeds or planting stock? Yes / No — the Organic Fraud Prevention Plan is not applicable (stop here; you do not need to fill out the rest of the form) / N/A — I don't grow perennial crops or harvest wild crops. | Partial | P3 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_areas` | A DIVERGENCE, not a missing field. OTCO lets a perennial or wild-crop grower who buys no certified organic inputs declare the whole plan not applicable and stop. Trazo's G2.0 has `allows_not_applicable=False` on purpose — the federal Common OSP Section 2 offers no N/A, because SOE applies § 205.201(a)(3) to every certified operation — so the same grower answers all three pages, briefly (the `none` risk area, the mitigations they actually run, the review cadence). The packet therefore carries a full plan where OTCO would have accepted a stopped form, and nothing on the packet says this is deliberate, so a reviewer may read the extra pages as the operation misjudging its own scope. The three facts OTCO's gate turns on — perennial system (G4.0), wild crop (W2.0), certified inputs purchased (G3.0/G3.2) — are all in the plan but are never stated together. **Fix:** Do NOT add an N/A gate to G2.0. For an OTCO packet, state on 04-coverage-and-scope.pdf (or in the G2.0 module header) that the plan answers the fraud-prevention module in full under the federal template even where OTCO's OFPP would accept "not applicable", and print the three trigger facts beside it so the reviewer sees why the pages are short. |
| 1-4 | Does your operation already have an Organic Fraud Prevention Plan? No — complete this module / Yes — plan is attached; you can skip the rest of this module if your plan includes all the required sections, and complete any that are missing. | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_plan_upload` · `company.Establishment.fraud_prevention_plan_document` · `company.Establishment.fraud_prevention_plan_date` · `company.Establishment.ofpp_on_file` | Reused from WSDA §P 1 (P2). An operation with a plan written elsewhere can attach it (`fraud_plan_upload`, or the farm profile's `fraud_prevention_plan_document`, which the readiness check accepts as "OFPP on file" alongside a completed G2.0), but no upload reaches `generate_osp_packet` — `osp_module_pdf` skips `kind in ("info", "upload")` and only parcel maps are written into the ZIP. OTCO's "Yes — attached" is therefore a statement the packet cannot back. **Fix:** Reuse §P 1 — carry module uploads into the packet ZIP the way `parcels/maps/` already travels, and print "plan attached: <filename>, dated <fraud_prevention_plan_date>" in G2.0's header when either upload exists. |

For a parcel that IS container production, none of the planting-date, materials or contamination-removal statements are captured. Re-judged 2026-11-10: A9 cites the same question as covered, and the No does print. **Fix:** When the production system is not in-ground (see F3), add `container_planting_date`, a materials statement (textarea or upload), and a contamination-removal description; print under §G. |
| Affidavit A | This affidavit pertains to the following parcel: name; block/lot; acreage; street address; city/county/state/country; and geographic coordinates or APN/Section-Township-Range. | Partial | P2 | `parcel_application.affidavit_card` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit (field_name, field_acres, parcel_legal_description)` | `field_name`, `field_acres`, and a free-text `parcel_legal_description` (which can hold APN/STR/coordinates) exist; there is no block/lot field and no address/city/county/state/country fields at all, and none of it is prefilled from the `Parcel` it concerns. **Fix:** Prefill §A from the `Parcel` (name, acres, APN/STR, address, county) as suggestions the signer confirms; add a `parcel_address` text field. |
| Affidavit B | I have direct and comprehensive knowledge of the activities and materials applied to the parcel from [date] through [date]. I have this knowledge because: I owned the parcel / I managed the parcel / Other (describe). | Partial | P2 | `parcel_application.affidavit_card` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.management_period_start` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.management_period_end` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.landowner_name` | The knowledge period (`management_period_start`/`management_period_end`) is captured. The basis of knowledge — owned, managed, or other — is not an explicit field; a reader can only infer it from whether `landowner_name` differs from the signer, which is a guess, not an attestation. **Fix:** Add `signer_basis` {owner, manager, other} and `signer_basis_other`; print it. |
| Affidavit C | Attestation of material use during the knowledge period (excluding anything more than 3 years ago): no materials of any kind were used / all materials used are listed in the Table of Materials Used / all materials used are listed on attached pages. Signature block: Name, Title, Company, Email, Phone, Signature, Date; and the 18 U.S.C. § 1001 false-statement notice. | Partial | P2 | `parcel_application.affidavit_card` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.no_materials_applied` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.attestation_text` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit.signed_document` | The tri-state attestation (`no_materials_applied` = True/False/unanswered) is honestly modeled and the scanned signature upload exists, along with name, phone and signed date — but Title, Company and Email have no fields, and the stored attestation text is MOFGA's wording rather than CCOF's own (CCOF does accept alternative documents, so this is not disqualifying by itself). **Fix:** Add `signer_title`, `signer_company`, `signer_email`; optionally store a `attestation_template = 'ccof'` variant carrying CCOF's exact wording when the certifier is CCOF. |
| Affidavit D | Table of Materials Used: Full Product Name, Full Manufacturer Name, Application Date(s), Type. | Partial | P2 | `parcel_application.affidavit_card` · `certifications.models.LandownerAffidavit (yearly_history)` | `yearly_history` rows carry year, land use, product (inputs), manufacturer and application date — three of the four columns. There is no `Type` column (fertilizer / herbicide / seed treatment, etc.). **Fix:** Add `material_type` (choices mirroring CCOF's list) to the row; print it. |

> Not reproduced since 2026-11-11: the packet and the copy sheet name this form and send the operation to the agent's own copy; they print none of the rows below and do not link the file. The rows record the edition read on 2026-10-01. Basis: WSDA Organic Program, email to Trazo, received by 2026-11-09: "Our fee forms are updated regularly. Inputting it in your system would potentially cause an operation to use an outdated form." The fee form is sent with the renewal application and is not published on WSDA's website.

| Header (business, contact, certificate) | Business Name; Name; Email; Cert No; Phone. | Covered | — | `company.Company.name` · `company.Establishment.contact_person` · `company.Establishment.contact_email` · `certifications.OrganicSystemPlan.approval_certificate_number` | — |
| 1 | Gross annual income received in the last calendar year. | Partial | P2 | `history.SalesRecord.sale_amount` | 02 totals the sales invoiced as organic and dated in the prior calendar year, and says it is not reconciled and not AGR 2521's figure (run 3, R3-03). WSDA asks for income RECEIVED from organic crops, products or services, which counts payments, not invoices, and includes services. Trazo's subtotal counts each sale by the date on its sale record, so a sale dated in the year and paid later is in it and money received in the year for an earlier sale is not; 02 says the subtotal counts sale dates, not payments. (Until 2026-11-04 this row and 02 said settlements after 31 December were left out, which was untrue.) **Fix:** Record payment dates on sales, total income received in the calendar year, and state any services income the operation enters. |

| 3 | Late fee ($100 for each month after March 1). | Out of scope | — | — | A payment owed to WSDA. |
| 4 | How will you be submitting your application packet and fee form/payment? Together hard copy / both hard copy under separate cover / application forms by email and fee form and payment by mail. | Out of scope | — | — | How the operation sends WSDA its application and its fee is its own logistics, chosen on the form. The form's own instruction is that the fee form and payment go by mail. (partial until 2026-11-04, though the filing method Trazo records is set after filing and describes Trazo's record, not this choice.) |

The form's own first checkbox ("Not Applicable; no materials/inputs are used") is how a grower with no inputs answers it, so in practice every grower files C11; it is also the form a certified operation files during the year to add a product to its current Materials List ("The products identified below are to be added to my current Materials List").

OTCO asks for ONE list covering every category; Trazo holds one list, read through `plan_materials()` from all four sources, and attests completeness four times, once per category (fertilizers and soil amendments; pest, disease and weed control; production aids; post-harvest contact materials) — a more demanding shape than OTCO's single list, and a reviewer can see which class was left unattested. Both exist only on operator-entered rows, and neither reaches the module PDF: `display()` prints name — manufacturer — identifier and nothing about use, so the list a reviewer reads has an empty Intended Use column on every row. The workbook prints the reason (or, for an event-derived row with no plan entry, the event type word — "Fertilizer", "Pest control"); a catalog-attached row with no operator entry and no logged application prints nothing anywhere. **Fix:** Print `category` (falling back to `reason_for_use`, then the event-type word) beside each row in the module PDF; require `category` on a catalog attach, the same way the "Instructions (all input materials)" fix requires `status`. |

The handling half has a real answer: `process_flow` is a required narrative — the handling process written out in order from harvest to shipment — and it prints, which is a written procedure by any reading. The production half does not: `fraud_plan_upload` is scoped to a fraud-prevention plan and `facility_docs` invites a site map, process flow chart or handling SOPs but is optional; since 2026-10-01 a file uploaded for it rides in the packet (attachments/g6_4_handling/facility_docs/) and is named on the G6.4 page. ### R Wild Harvest

*AGR 2121 · R 02/25 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** Triggered when the operation harvests and distributes crops marketed as Wild Harvest from an un-cultivated or unmanaged site; most crop producer operations attest Not Applicable. CCOF's equivalent (W2.0, ORGB48) is a scope decision in ccof/scope.yaml, not a registered form.

**11 questions** — Covered 1 · Partial 3 · Not covered 7

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not applicable (section) | Not Applicable: My business does not harvest and distribute crops marketed as Wild Harvest. Skip to next section. | Covered | — | — | — |
| 1 | Describe the natural environment of the harvested area (e.g. scrub steppe, oak-chaparral woodland, deciduous hardwood forest). | Partial | P2 | `w2_0_wild_crop.wild_crop_description` | The module's single combined textarea invites an environment description but does not separately require it — a farm could fill in only sustainability practices and leave the environment description out entirely. **Fix:** Split `wild_crop_description` into distinct fields for natural environment, harvest method, and sustainability practices, matching WSDA's R1-R3 breakdown. |
| 2 | Describe how each wild crop will be harvested. | Partial | P2 | `w2_0_wild_crop.wild_crop_description` | Same combined-textarea limitation as R1 — harvest method per crop has no dedicated field. **Fix:** Same split as R1. |
| 3 | How do you ensure harvesting practices are not environmentally detrimental to the wild crop habitat? | Partial | P2 | `w2_0_wild_crop.wild_crop_description` | Sustainability of the harvest is the one part the field's own prompt text explicitly invites ('...how harvest sustainability is protected'), so this is the best-covered of the R1-R3 group — but it still shares one field with two other distinct questions. **Fix:** Same split as R1. |
| 4 | How do you monitor the health of the wild crop, how often is the monitoring performed, and what records are maintained to document your monitoring practices? | Not covered | P2 | — | No field asks about ongoing health monitoring, its frequency, or records kept — the module has no monitoring concept at all, unlike the cultivated-crop modules' `fertility_monitoring` / `monitoring_frequency` pattern. **Fix:** Add `wild_crop_monitoring` and `wild_crop_monitoring_frequency` fields mirroring G4.0's monitoring page. |

| 6 | Describe how you determine if there are rare, threatened, or endangered plants and animals present on the sites from which wild crops are harvested. | Not covered | P2 | — | No field asks how the operation determines whether rare, threatened or endangered species are present on a harvest site. **Fix:** Add a `species_determination_method` textarea. |

## Forms Trazo does not register

CCOF's Guide routes by activity, so what is absent is as readable as what is present.
A **decision** is an answer; a **gap** is a debt, and names where it is triggered from.

### Gaps

| Form | Triggered from | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Co-Packer Application (ORGB26) | G7.0 C — packing into a brand owned by another company | Trazo does not generate this form. An operation that packs its crop into a brand owned by another company files the Co-Packer Application with CCOF directly. |
| Exempt Handler Affidavit (NOPB107) | G6.1 A2/A3 (uncertified harvester or transporter); G6.2 A (uncertified storage); G6.5 A1 (uncertified supplier) | Trazo does not generate this form. Where an uncertified harvester, transporter, storage site or supplier handles this operation's crop, the affidavit is filed with CCOF directly. |
| IS – Independent & Off-Site Storage (IS) | C1 routing (stores crops at a non-certified facility that does not open, re-label or process the product, one per facility) and the C7 §7.7 storage table documentation column IS | Trazo does not generate this sheet. It is answered and signed by the manager of the uncertified warehouse or storage facility, and a copy is kept by both parties. Where this operation stores crop it still owns at such a facility, the plan records the facility by name and location in its storage section; the facility's own sheet is filed with the agent directly. |
| Private Label Agreement (PLA) (Private Label Agreement) | C8 §8.3 — packing organic crop into another company's brand or label when that brand owner is not itself certified | Trazo does not generate this agreement. The plan records, in its labeling section, that crop leaves the operation under a buyer's label and the label claim the operation makes; the brand owner's certificate, or the agreement between the operation and an uncertified brand owner, is collected by the operation and filed with the agent directly. |
| Organic Label Approval Verification (AGR 2724) | AGR 2121 §N (labeling) — any label bearing an organic claim or the agent's mark | Trazo does not generate this form, and label artwork is not attached to this plan. The labeling section records how product is identified and what claims are used; the artwork itself goes to the agent directly for approval. |

### Deliberately not built

| Form | Reason |
|---|---|
| W2.0 Wild Crop Harvesting (ORGB48) | Trazo ships an N/A-attestable stub module so a crop grower can record that wild-crop harvesting does not apply, which is what a crop-scope OSP needs. An operation that does harvest wild crop files the full W2.0 with CCOF directly: its designated-area, 36-month harvest-site history and harvest-sustainability content is outside this plan's scope of cultivated orchard and berry ground. |
| Handler / Processor OSP forms (H-series) (ORGB32) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (CCOF G6.4). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product. A farm needing the H-series files it with its certifier directly. |
| Livestock OSP forms (L-series) (Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms) | Crop scope only. Nothing in the data model represents animals, feed, origin of livestock or living conditions, and pretending otherwise on a form would be worse than the absence. |
| Retail Establishment forms (R-series) (R1.0–R5.0) | Retail and restaurant operations are not producers. Out of scope by definition. |
| OCal Cultivator and Handler forms (OCal C-series / OCal H-series) | OCal is California's comparable-to-organic standard for cannabis. Different crop, different statute, different market. |
| Annual ROC™ Renewal Contract (Annual ROC Renewal Contract) | The renewal for an operation certified both organic and Regenerative Organic Certified. Its National Organic Program section asks what the Annual Renewal Contract asks, and the packet supports that one; the Regenerative Organic renewal itself is filed with the Regenerative Organic Alliance, a private standard this packet does not assess. |
| Annual OCal Renewal Contract (Annual OCal Renewal Contract) | The renewal of OCal certification, California's standard for cannabis; out of scope with the OCal forms. |
| COR (Canada) Handler forms (COR H-series) | Canadian Organic Regime equivalence. Out of scope while the market is US crop producers. |
| Global Market Access Application; Mexico Compliance Program; NOP Import Certificate Request (GMA04) | Export-programme enrolment and the certificates themselves are transactions between the operation and CCOF. Trazo captures the export and import questions the Common OSP asks (destination countries, certificate types, request-and-retain process, port integrity) inside G8.0 page C, which is the recordkeeping half — it does not file for the certificates. |
| Contracted Partner Program Application (Guide item 17) | An arrangement where a CCOF-certified customer manages the grower's certification. A grower in that programme has no OSP of their own to keep. |
| Certification Transfer Form (Certification Transfer Form) | Filed by an operation moving between certifying agents, which is a one-time transfer arrangement between the operation and the two agents rather than a fact about how the operation is farmed. An operation transferring certification files it directly. |
| Organic Fraud Prevention Plan (ORGB108) | CCOF publishes this worksheet with its handler and retail OSP forms. It is written for an operation that receives organic product from suppliers: a supply chain map, checks at receiving and a supplier approval program. This plan states the operation's own fraud prevention practices under 7 CFR 205.201(a)(3) in its Monitoring and Organic Fraud Prevention section. An operation CCOF asks for this worksheet completes it with CCOF directly. |
| T&C – Terms and Conditions (T&C) | The certification services and trademark-use terms (rev. 2023/09/14) that bind the operation to its certifying agent. They carry no signature block of their own: they are incorporated by reference and accepted by signing the Operation Information affirmations or the OSP Update Application and Agreement. Nothing is drafted from the operation's records. |
| C1 – Crop Activities Checklist (C1) | The checklist that routes an operation to the plan sections its activities require. The packet's coverage page performs that routing for this operation in the agent's own form numbers, so the checklist is not reproduced as a separate document; the operation ticks it directly when the agent asks for it. |
| M1 – Mushroom Production (M1) | Applies to an operation that produces mushrooms, spawn or mycelial biomass. Mushroom growing is an operation Trazo does not serve: it is built for orchards and field crops grown in the ground, and has no mushroom substrate, spawn or growing-room records. An operation that produces mushrooms completes M1 with the agent directly. |
| A1 – Aquaponics, Container, and Greenhouse Production (A1) | Applies to crops grown in containers or aquaponics, to seedlings or transplants grown indoors for sale, to indoor structures that are not on certified land, and to greenhouses shared by organic and non-organic production. Crops grown in the ground under a high tunnel or hoop house do not need it. This plan does not describe those systems, so an operation that has any of them completes A1 with the agent directly. |
| C13 – Producer Group Operation (C13) | Applies to a grower cooperative certified as one multi-site operation under an internal control system (7 CFR 205.201(c)). This plan describes a single operation; a producer group files C13 with the agent directly. |
| C14 – Incubator Operation (C14) | Applies to an incubator operation that assists start-up farms with access to land. This plan describes a single operation managing its own parcels; an incubator files C14 with the agent directly. |
| W1 – Wild Crop Harvest (W1) | Trazo ships an N/A-attestable stub module so a crop grower can record that wild-crop harvesting does not apply, which is what a crop-scope plan needs. An operation that does harvest wild crop files the full W1 with the agent directly: its designated-area, harvest-site history and harvest-sustainability content is outside this plan's scope of cultivated orchard and berry ground. |
| Commercial Availability Form (CAF) (CAF) | A worksheet documenting one commercial-availability search, one form for each non-organic agricultural product or ingredient. It is written mainly for handlers; a farm may use it to document the search for non-organic seed, which has to be made each time non-organic seed is planted. The plan records whether a search precedes the use of non-organic seed and which search records the operation keeps; the worksheets themselves are the operation's own records, kept for inspection rather than generated by the plan. |
| Contact Change Form (Contact Change Form) | Notifies the agent of a change to the operation's contacts and their permissions. It is an administrative update to the agent's client record and is filed by the operation directly. |
| Crop Input Verification Evaluation (Manufacturer Declaration for Crop Inputs) (Crop Input Verification Evaluation) | A declaration the MANUFACTURER or its legal designee completes and signs about one input material — ingredients, extraction methods, excluded-methods status — valid for five years. The operation requests it from the manufacturer for any material that is not listed by a third-party review agency and keeps it with its input records; the operation cannot author a manufacturer's own attestation. |
| Land Transfer Form (Land Transfer Form) | Transfers a parcel between two operations both certified by this agent, when the field was inspected within the last twelve months, so that the parcel is added without a new inspection. It is signed by both the releasing and the receiving operation and filed with the agent directly; the receiving operation's plan records the parcel once it is on its certificate. |
| Manure Verification (Manure Verification) | A statement the manure SUPPLIER completes about the source and treatment of purchased manure. The plan records whether raw manure is applied, the pre-harvest interval it is held to and how water contamination is prevented, in its soil fertility section; the supplier's own statement is collected by the operation and kept with its input records. |
| Wood and Livestock Bedding Verification (Wood and Livestock Bedding Verification) | A statement the SUPPLIER of wood products or livestock bedding completes about treatments and additives. The plan lists such materials on the operation's materials list; the supplier's own statement is collected by the operation and kept with its input records. |
| OTCO Fee Schedule 2026 (OTCO Fee Schedule 2026) | The agent's published fee schedule, used with the renewal application to compute the certification fee from reported gross organic sales. It is the agent's own document, not a form the operation completes. |
| Handler Organic System Plan (AGR 2180) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (WSDA Crop Producer OSP §K Storage, §L Post-Harvest). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product — WSDA certifies handling under a separate Handler OSP (product flow, equipment cleaning and sanitation). A farm needing the Handler OSP files it with WSDA Organic Program directly. |
| Processed Product Application (AGR 2523) | Application to add a processed (multi-ingredient) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope excluded above — Trazo does not carry a farm into a handler-scope application. |
| Handled Product Application (AGR 2524) | Application to add a handled (single-ingredient, minimally processed) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope exclusion as AGR 2523. |
| Multi- and Single-Ingredient Processed Product Formulation (AGR 2178 / AGR 2179) | Ingredient-percentage formulation worksheets for a handler's processed-product recipe. Handler-side; a grower shipping raw or lightly-handled crop has no 'formulation' to declare. Same handler/processor scope exclusion. |
| Natural Flavor Questionnaire (AGR 2700) | Characterizes a purchased natural-flavor ingredient's own processing, for a handler's product formulation. Handler-side ingredient sourcing; same scope exclusion. |
| Non-Organic Ingredient Affidavit (AGR 2252) | Attests to a nonorganic ingredient used in a handler's multi-ingredient product. Handler-side product formulation, not something a crop grower selling raw or lightly-handled produce needs. |
| Ingredient Commercial Availability (AGR 2251) | WSDA's handler-side commercial-availability worksheet for a nonorganic ingredient in a processed product. Handler scope; same exclusion. It is not the grower-side seed and planting-stock commercial-availability search, which this plan does answer. |
| New Application for Organic Certification (AGR 2500) | The one-time application an operation files to enter the organic program — contacts, sites, products and the signed agreement. Trazo serves already-certified operations preparing an annual renewal, so the plan starts from an existing certification rather than establishing one. A first-time applicant files this directly. |
| Annual Renewal Application (Renewal application) | The renewal application a certified operation files with WSDA by March 1 each year ("your business must renew your application by March 1 each year"). WSDA does not publish it among its blank forms, so it is not reproduced here. The year's changes it asks for are on the annual update pages of this packet, and the site update (AGR 2516) and renewal fee (AGR 2521) forms are listed with it. |
| Organic Contact Information (AGR 2515) | Names and contact details for the people the agent corresponds with. The plan records the operation's responsible person and prints it on the packet cover; keeping the agent's own contact roster current is done with the agent directly. |
| New Applicant Fee (AGR 2499) | A fee paid by the operation to the agent. It sets what certification costs, not how the operation farms. |

## What Trazo asks that the registered forms do not

Not gaps — questions the federal Common OSP or the regulation itself asks for, which a
certifier's own grower overlay leaves implicit. Stated per agent: a question one asks and
the other does not is the most informative row here.

### CCOF

| Question | Why it has no CCOF counterpart |
|---|---|
| `certification_contract.contract_scopes` | Maps to the Contract's cover-page guide selection ('Guide to Grower OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Handler OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Retail Establishment OSP Forms') rather than to any of the Contract's own lettered/numbered questions (A-H); Trazo captures the choice as a structured field instead of a forms checklist. |
| `certification_contract.history_currently_suspended` | OTCO O1 D-2B's precondition (a request to reinstate an operation suspended today). CCOF's Contract has no reinstatement question. |
| `certification_contract.history_not_sold_since_revocation` | OTCO O1 D-3A (new in OTCO's rev. 2026/03/25). CCOF's Contract asks for no affirmation after a revocation. |
| `certification_contract.history_not_sold_since_suspension` | OTCO O1 D-2A (new in OTCO's rev. 2026/03/25). CCOF's Contract asks for no affirmation after a suspension. |
| `certification_contract.history_outstanding_noncompliances` | OTCO O1 D-1E. CCOF's Contract asks only whether a certification was surrendered or an application withdrawn with noncompliances outstanding (D5b, D5d), not whether any is outstanding today; asked on the same page for OTCO. |
| `certification_contract.history_request_reinstatement` | OTCO O1 D-2B, the request that NOP reinstate a suspended operation (§ 205.662(f)(1)). CCOF's Contract has no such request. |
| `certification_contract.history_this_agent_records` | An info line on page C, not a question: it says the current agent's notices already print on 02s with their letters, so the upload is for earlier agencies' letters. CCOF D6 is answered by the explanation and the upload. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_plan_upload` | Optional upload for a written fraud-prevention plan. CCOF's G8.0 D references an external 'Fraud Prevention Plan worksheet' as guidance and reserves the right to request one for complex operations, but the grower form itself does not ask for an attachment. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_risk_areas`; not a separate CCOF question — G8.0 D1 is a fixed checklist of scenarios with no open-ended 'other'. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_accuracy_process` | Who keeps the OSP accurate, and how. The Certification Contract B2 asks only review FREQUENCY (annually/quarterly/monthly/other); it does not ask who performs the review or how, which this question captures beyond what either form requests. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_implementation_monitoring_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `osp_implementation_monitoring`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.product_testing_detail` | Free-text elaboration (what is tested, and how often) for the `product_testing` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not asked as its own CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.residue_detection_response` | How the operation responds when its own testing detects a pesticide residue. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P 4b; CCOF's G8.0 fraud-prevention section lists product testing as a practice and never asks the method or the response. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.residue_screening_method` | The screening or analysis behind the operation's own product testing (laboratory, residue panel). Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P 4a; CCOF's G8.0 fraud-prevention section lists product testing as a practice and never asks the method or the response. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.supplier_approval_controls` | How suppliers are approved and followed. Asked by OTCO's fraud prevention plan (2-2) and WSDA AGR 2121 P5; CCOF G8.0 D2 asks only how current organic status is verified, which supplier_certificate_review_frequency answers. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.supplier_approval_controls_other` | Describes an "other" answer to `supplier_approval_controls` above; same reason. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.supplier_approval_procedure_upload` | A written supplier approval procedure. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P5 ("procedures are attached"); no CCOF form asks for one. |
| `g3_0_seeds.buyer_search_documents` | The buyer's own commercial-availability search on contract-supplied seed. OTCO C3 3.3-3 asks it; CCOF's G3.0 B2 names the case only as a search method. |
| `g3_0_seeds.farm_grown_processing_contracted` | Contracted processing (seed cleaning) of farm-grown seed or transplants. OTCO C3 3.2-3 asks it; CCOF's G3.0 has no such question. |
| `g3_0_seeds.farm_grown_processing_description` | The detail of the contracted processing above; same reason. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_source` | Seed provenance (saved, purchased, contract-supplied). WSDA AGR 2121 A1 and OTCO C3 3.2-2 ask it; CCOF's G3.0 asks organic status and treatment only. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_treatment_applied_by` | Who applies the seed treatment. WSDA AGR 2121 A2b and A3c ask it; CCOF's G3.0 D does not. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_treatment_types` | An inventory of treatment types. OTCO C3 3.5-1 asks it; CCOF's G3.0 D asks the allowance basis and the materials list, not the types. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_verification_method` | How certified organic seed is verified. WSDA AGR 2121 A2a asks it; CCOF's G3.0 A1 records the status and never asks the method. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seeds_additional_notes` | A free-text notes field. WSDA AGR 2121 A4 offers one; CCOF's G3.0 has none. |
| `g3_0_seeds.untreated_seed_documentation` | Documents behind an untreated claim. OTCO C3 3.5 requires them; CCOF's G3.0 A1 takes the checkbox alone. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedling_facility_certified` | Whether that facility is certified; OTCO C3 3.2-1 prints it as a requirement; same reason. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedling_growing_location` | The location of the seedling growing facility; same reason. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_grown_on_site` | Where own seedlings are grown. WSDA AGR 2121 B2a and OTCO C3 3.2-1 ask it; CCOF's G3.0 A2 sends own seedlings to G3.1, which Trazo does not model as a form. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_labeling_description` | How sold seedlings are labeled. WSDA AGR 2121 B3a asks it; same reason. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_sold_as_organic` | Selling annual seedlings as organic. WSDA AGR 2121 B3 asks it; CCOF's G3.0 has no seedling-sale question. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_upload` | A plan-level file, tied to no supplier and no purchase. Since 2026-11-05 the certificate each seedling supplier's purchase needs is the copy in the supplier register, which the G3.0a supplier panel (`seedling_suppliers_panel`) reads and the packet carries under suppliers/. A file uploaded here still rides in the packet under attachments/ and is listed on G3.0a; it answers no form item by itself. |

| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_additional_notes` | A free-text notes field. WSDA AGR 2121 C5 offers one; CCOF's G3.0 has none. |

This is the § 205.103 source-and- planting record (where the stock came from, where and when it was planted) Trazo captures for the invoice-to-block trace an inspector performs — beyond anything G3.0 itself asks. |

| `g9_0_facility_pest.facility_pest_records_upload` | Files for the facility pest records the plan says are kept (`pest_control_records`). CCOF's G6.2 B9 asks how pest control material use is recorded, not for the records themselves; these are the § 205.103 records an inspector reviews on site. The upload lets the packet carry them beside modules/G9_0.pdf. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_name` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_notified` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning (§205.271 notification requirement). |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_monitoring_frequency` | How often facility pests are monitored. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 M3; same reason. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_monitoring_practices` | How facility pest pressure is monitored. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 M3; CCOF asks facility pest controls in G6.2 B3 and B4, not the monitoring practice. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation` | How the operation documents that prevention and mechanical controls were not enough before a material is applied (the § 205.271(a)-(d) sequence; WSDA AGR 2121 M asks it). CCOF's Materials Application §F and §G list the materials themselves, which the materials list answers. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation_other` | Companion detail field to preventive_measures_documentation, which the Materials Application register (ref F) already cites for the National List material-type table it maps to — this free-text "other" elaboration has no separate CCOF counterpart of its own. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.uses_pest_control_company` | §205.271 requires notifying any contracted pest control operator that the site is certified organic. CCOF's G6.2 form (the only grower form whose B3-B9 substantively maps to G9.0) does not ask whether a contracted pest control company is used as its own distinct checkbox. Trazo asks it directly as a named-company gate. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_detail` | Same reason as fumigant_prohibited_material_used — it is the free-text continuation of that duplicate question, not something ORGB41 asks for. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_used` | ORGB41 (the Grower Materials Application) never asks about fumigant or prohibited-material history — that disclosure belongs to the Parcel Application's land history (ORGB49 §F4/§F8) and the Affidavit of Land History. This restates the same § 205.202(b) fact a second time at the operation level rather than filling a gap CCOF's materials form leaves open. |
| `parcel_application.certification_status_requested` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 4. CCOF grants its transitional status on its own after review (ORGB49 §B) and does not ask for it on the parcel application. |
| `parcel_application.certified_operation_name` | Asked by OTCO C2 2.1-7 ('provide the certified operation's name and certification agency') and WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6 ('operation name'). CCOF F2 asks only whether the parcel is currently certified and §G asks for the certificate itself; the operation named on that certificate is read off the copy, never asked as a field. |
| `parcel_application.full_prior_site_area` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6b asks whether the whole previously or currently certified site is applied for or only a portion. CCOF's Parcel Application asks no such question: F2 sends a currently certified parcel to section G, and a part of a parcel with a different history is a separate application. |
| `parcel_application.landowner_address` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. Not asked by CCOF. |
| `parcel_application.landowner_email` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. Not asked by CCOF. |
| `parcel_application.landowner_name` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. CCOF's Parcel Application asks none of it; its affidavits name whoever attests to past land use, a different person. |
| `parcel_application.landowner_phone` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. Not asked by CCOF. |
| `parcel_application.lease_management_detail` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. Not asked by CCOF. |
| `parcel_application.location_zip` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 2 and OTCO C2 2.1 4). CCOF's A3 asks street, city, county, state and country, with no ZIP code. |
| `parcel_application.no_inputs_within_tenure` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 13 ('N/A — No input materials have been applied while under my management'). CCOF's Parcel Application asks about PROHIBITED material only (F4, the date of the last prohibited application, answered by dlpm_none_within_tenure and the land history); it never asks whether any input at all was applied. |
| `parcel_application.operation_export_answer` | Prints the operation's G8.0 export answer on the parcel page for WSDA AGR 2264 ref 9, which asks it per site. |
| `parcel_application.site_tenure` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7 and OTCO C2 2.1-6 ask whether the operation owns, leases or manages the parcel; CCOF's Parcel Application (ORGB49) asks only when the operator began managing it (F1), never the tenure. |
| `parcel_application.site_tenure_other` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7 and OTCO C2 2.1-6 ask whether the operation owns, leases or manages the parcel; CCOF's Parcel Application (ORGB49) asks only when the operator began managing it (F1), never the tenure. |
| `parcel_application.transitional_certificate_before_harvest` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 4a, which only a transitional application reaches. |
| `parcel_application.treated_lumber_contact_prevention` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (how contact between existing treated lumber and organic crops or livestock is prevented). CCOF asks whether treated lumber is present and for its description and install date (Parcel Application A10 / A10a) and, on G6.0 B2, the going-forward replacement policy — never the measure that keeps installed lumber off organic crop and soil. |
| `parcel_application.treated_seed_detail` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 11a (brand of treatment and planting date). |
| `parcel_application.treated_seed_planted` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 11 for the site under the applicant's management. CCOF asks about seed farm-wide on G3.0, not per parcel. |

### OTCO

| Question | Why it has no OTCO counterpart |
|---|---|
| `certification_contract.history_this_agent_records` | An info line on page C, not a question: it says the current agent's notices already print on 02s with their letters, so the upload is for earlier agencies' letters. D-7 is answered by the explanation and the upload. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.residue_detection_response` | How the operation responds when its own testing detects a pesticide residue. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P 4b; OTCO's OFPP asks whether SUPPLIERS send residue results and notify the operation in writing of a residue (an option of the supplier-approval list), never the operation's own testing method or response. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.residue_screening_method` | The screening or analysis behind the operation's own product testing (laboratory, residue panel). Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P 4a; OTCO's OFPP asks whether SUPPLIERS send residue results and notify the operation in writing of a residue (an option of the supplier-approval list), never the operation's own testing method or response. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.supplier_approval_procedure_upload` | A written supplier approval procedure. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 P5; OTCO's fraud prevention plan 2-2 asks which controls are used (supplier_approval_controls), not for the procedure as a document. |
| `g3_0_seeds.grafting_practices` | Grafting practices. CCOF G3.0 E1a asks it; no form in the OTCO crop set mentions grafting. |
| `g3_0_seeds.grafts_stock` | Whether the operation grafts planting stock. No OTCO crop form asks about grafting at all — not C3, not C11 (whose category list runs fertilizers, pest and disease materials, compost and manure, inoculants, planting mixes, seed treatments, cleaners and sanitizers, adjuvants, mulches), not C7. CCOF asks it at G3.0 E1 and WSDA's §C header defines its scope as "planting or grafting stock"; OTCO's 2025 form set does not raise it. Grafting wax, tape and sealant would reach OTCO only as C11 material rows. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_treatment_applied_by` | Who applies the seed treatment. WSDA AGR 2121 A2b and A3c ask it; OTCO's C3 3.5 asks the types and the C11 listing. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_verification_method` | How certified organic seed is verified. WSDA AGR 2121 A2a asks it; OTCO's C3 3.1-1 records the status only. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seeds_additional_notes` | A free-text notes field. WSDA AGR 2121 A4 offers one; OTCO's C3 has none. |
| `g3_0_seeds.treatment_verification` | On what basis the seed-treatment materials are allowed (an OMRI or WSDA listing, or written certifier approval). OTCO's C3 §3.5 asks the operation to IDENTIFY its seed treatments (pelletization, coating, inoculant, fungicide, insecticide, disinfectant) and to carry them onto the C11 Crop Materials List; it never asks the allowance basis on C3, because C11 itself has a "Third Party Review Agency (OMRI / WSDA / Other)" column per material and demands a label or photo for anything not OMRI- or WSDA-listed. So OTCO answers CCOF D1's question on the materials list rather than on the seed form. CCOF asks it directly at G3.0 D1, where it is registered `covered`; the C11 register is where the OTCO-side citation belongs. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_labeling_description` | How sold seedlings are labeled. WSDA AGR 2121 B3a asks it; OTCO's C3 3.2-2 asks only whether farm-grown seedlings are sold. |
| `g3_1_seedlings.seedlings_upload` | A plan-level file, tied to no supplier and no purchase. Since 2026-11-05 the certificate each seedling supplier's purchase needs is the copy in the supplier register, which the G3.0a supplier panel (`seedling_suppliers_panel`) reads and the packet carries under suppliers/. A file uploaded here still rides in the packet under attachments/ and is listed on G3.0a; it answers no form item by itself. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.first_organic_harvest_handling` | How growth present on nonorganic stock is kept out of the first organic harvest. CCOF G3.0 A3a(i) asks it; OTCO does not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.first_organic_harvest_handling_other` | The other-handling detail of the question above; same reason. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.nonorganic_stock_for_organic_crop` | Whether nonorganic stock grows a crop sold as organic. CCOF G3.0 A3a asks it; OTCO's C3 does not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.organic_management_start_date` | When organic management of planting stock that will be SOLD as organic began — the start of the § 205.204(a)(4) twelve-month clock. C3 §3.2 asks only whether farm-grown perennial stock is used "for planting or sale" (cited at 3.2-2 through `stock_sold_as_organic`) and never follows the sale with the one-year requirement, the date, or an attestation. CCOF asks it at G3.0 A3b and WSDA at §C 4a. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.organic_stock_treatments` | Treatment of ORGANIC planting stock. WSDA AGR 2121 C2b asks it; OTCO's C3 3.5 is about seed treatments. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.organic_stock_verification_method` | How organic planting stock is verified. WSDA AGR 2121 C2a asks it; OTCO's C3 3.1-3 records the status only. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_additional_notes` | A free-text notes field. WSDA AGR 2121 C5 offers one; OTCO's C3 has none. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.resold_stock_labeling_description` | How resold planting stock is labeled. WSDA AGR 2121 C4b asks it; OTCO's C3 does not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_treatment_applied_by` | Who applied a treatment to nonorganic stock. WSDA AGR 2121 C3c asks it; OTCO's C3 does not ask about stock treatment. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_treatments` | Whether non-organic planting stock was treated before or at delivery (fungicide dip, wax, root gel). C3 §3.5 SEED TREATMENTS is scoped to seed — "Identify all seed treatments in use" — and 3.1-5's documentation question is about the inputs a CONTRACT GROWER used in production, not about a nursery's post-harvest dip on stock bought off the shelf. WSDA asks the stock case at §C 3c; CCOF and OTCO do not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.twelve_month_attestation` | The operator's confirmation that no planting stock is sold or labelled organic before twelve months of organic management. Companion to `organic_management_start_date`; same reason — C3 stops at "for planting or sale". |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.twelve_month_records_description` | Records behind the 12-month clock. WSDA AGR 2121 C4a asks it; OTCO's C3 3.2-2 asks only what is farm grown for sale. |

| `g4_0_rotation_soil.fertility_components` | The major components of the soil-fertility and crop-nutrient plan (crop residue, cover crops, compost, manure, mined minerals, blended or foliar fertilizers, inoculants, fertigation, rotation…). C4 has no "how do you manage soil health / fertility" checklist: its sections are tillage and erosion (4.1), rotation and in-lieu practices (4.2), manure (4.3), compost (4.4), micronutrients (4.5) and monitoring (4.6), and its § 205.203 header states the obligation without asking for an inventory of how it is met. OTCO reads the fertility INPUTS off the C11 Crop Materials List ("Intended Use: Fertility" column) and the fertility PRACTICES off 4.2–4.4. The word "fertilizer" appears on no other OTCO crop-OSP form except C9's list of materials used in NON-organic production. CCOF asks the checklist at G4.0 A2 and WSDA at §D 2, both `partial`. Micronutrients (4.5-1) are asked by their own question since 2026-11-05, not through this field. |

Magnesium sulfate, calcium chloride and potassium chloride are read off the C11 Crop Materials List. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 D4-D6a; superset for an OTCO plan, added 2026-11-05 (restricted-materials slice). |

Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 D4-D6a; superset for an OTCO plan, added 2026-11-05 (restricted-materials slice). |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_applied_inside_interval` | Whether manure-based compost is applied inside the 90 or 120 days. Asked by WSDA §D 9; OTCO C4 §4.4 asks how every compost is produced instead. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_documentation` | Whether the operator keeps the SUPPLIER's process description or analysis for purchased compost on file — the § 205.203(c)(2) evidence for a product the certifier cannot inspect at source. C4 §4.4 routes purchased compost to C11 ("I purchase compost (and/or tea) – Provide product information in Section C11"), and C11 collects product name, manufacturer, third-party review agency and intended use, with a label or photo for anything not OMRI- or WSDA-listed; it never asks the grower to hold the composter's temperature record or lab analysis. The only OTCO document that speaks to a supplier's process is the Crop Input Verification Evaluation, which the MANUFACTURER completes ("Manure – No additives or chemical treatments used") and which otco/scope.yaml excludes as a manufacturer's own attestation. So OTCO, like CCOF (whose register unmaps this field for the same reason), leaves the supplier evidence to the materials review; WSDA alone asks it, at AGR 2196's "How you ensure compliance" column. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_upload` | The attachment for `purchased_compost_documentation` above; same reason. (It would not reach a certifier in any case — `osp_module_pdf` skips `kind in ("info", "upload")`, and only parcel maps are written into the packet ZIP.) |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.soil_fertility_additional_notes` | A free-text notes field. WSDA §D 14 offers one; OTCO C4 has none. |

| `g4_2_natural_resources.irrigation_efficiency_monitoring` | How irrigation efficiency is checked. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 E10; OTCO C6 2a lists water conservation practices, soil-moisture monitoring among them, without asking how efficiency is checked. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.irrigation_efficiency_monitoring_other` | Describes an "other" answer to `irrigation_efficiency_monitoring` above; same reason. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.natural_resources_description` | A description of the operation's natural resources and biodiversity. Asked by CCOF G4.2 A1. OTCO C6 asks which practices maintain or improve natural resources and, at its end, for additional measures; it never asks for a description of the resources themselves. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.shared_irrigation_mitigation` | How contact with materials in shared irrigation water is prevented (CCOF G6.0 D5). OTCO C2 2.3-3 asks for the valves and backflow devices on the parcel map or a piping diagram, which `irrigation_piping_map_upload` takes; it never asks for a description of how contact is prevented. |

| `g5_0_pest.copper_accumulation_other` | OTCO's C5 does not ask about copper accumulation. OTCO reads copper products off the C11 Crop Materials List. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 H5/H5a; superset for an OTCO plan, added 2026-11-05 (restricted-materials slice). |
| `g5_0_pest.copper_accumulation_practices` | OTCO's C5 does not ask about copper accumulation. OTCO reads copper products off the C11 Crop Materials List. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 H5/H5a; superset for an OTCO plan, added 2026-11-05 (restricted-materials slice). |
| `g5_0_pest.disease_monitoring_frequency` | How often diseases are monitored. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 H2; same reason. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | How often pest, weed and disease monitoring is performed. C5 § 5.3 has exactly one question, the monitoring METHOD, and no follow-on about frequency; a full read of the form finds "how often" only at § 5.2 ("how often burning is conducted"), which is about residue burning, not monitoring, and is cited at C5 5.2-1 (type and frequency) as the frequency Trazo does NOT capture. WSDA asks this three times (F2/G2/H2); OTCO asks it never. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` | How monitoring RESULTS are recorded (§ 205.201(a)(3)). C5 asks nothing about records of any kind — recordkeeping is OTCO's separate C12 Crop Recordkeeping module, which the C1 checklist routes every grower to. C5 § 5.3's one question is about the method used to judge effectiveness, and citing a records field there would be the topic-adjacent citation the second trap in ../README.md describes. WSDA F6/G5/H4 ask a records question and decline to cite this field on an axis objection; OTCO gives no occasion to decide. |
| `g5_0_pest.pest_monitoring_frequency` | How often pests are monitored. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 G2; same reason. |
| `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_removal` | How plastic or synthetic mulch is removed from the field at season end (§ 205.206(c)(6)). C5's plastic-mulch question (5.1-5, "Do you use plastic mulch, landscape fabric, or other physical weed barriers?") routes a Yes to C11 — "include manufacturer and brand name on the C11 or provide a product label" — treating the barrier as a MATERIAL to be reviewed, and asks nothing about its removal. `plastic_mulch_used` is cited at 5.1-5; this follow-on is reachable only when that gate is yes and OTCO asks no question it would answer. CCOF G5.0 §A and WSDA F4/F5 both ask the removal condition and cite it. |
| `g5_0_pest.weed_monitoring_frequency` | How often weeds are monitored. Asked by WSDA AGR 2121 F2; OTCO C5 5.3-1 asks the monitoring method once for the whole plan. |
| `g6_0_production.dedicated_equipment_contamination_prevention` | How dedicated equipment is kept from prohibited materials and marked (WSDA I 1a). OTCO C9 does not ask it. |
| `g6_0_production.drift_agreements_upload` | Written agreements with neighbors, attached (CCOF G6.0 A2). OTCO C9 9.3-1 asks for the plan to mitigate drift, never for the agreements as attachments. |
| `g6_0_production.drift_response_procedure` | What the operation does when it suspects drift or contact with a prohibited substance has ALREADY happened — the § 205.400(f)(1) immediate-notification duty, plus sampling, quarantine and corrective action. C9 § 9.3 asks for PREVENTION and MITIGATION plans: "describe your plan to mitigate the drift risk" (9.3-1), "describe your plan to mitigate the risk of runoff" (9.3-2), "the steps you have taken to prevent contamination from roadside management" (9.3-3). Each is about keeping the substance off the land, and each is cited against the safeguards and buffer fields. Nothing on C9 — or on C2, whose buffer table C9 points to — asks what happens after a suspected event. This is the same line wsda/unmapped/g6_0_production.yaml draws for AGR 2264 ref 14's "risk prevention strategy", and the reason the field is not cited at 9.3-1 as a topic-adjacent answer: a response procedure is not a mitigation plan, and the register should not report it as one. CCOF G6.0 A2 cites it as a Trazo-only superset beside CCOF's ten drift checkboxes because CCOF's form opens with the instruction to notify CCOF immediately of drift; C9 carries no such instruction. |
| `g6_0_production.equipment_notes` | Free space for anything else about equipment (WSDA I 4). OTCO C9 has no such line. |
| `g6_0_production.roadside_agreement_upload` | A written agreement with the roadside manager, attached (CCOF G6.0 A2). OTCO C9 9.3-1 asks for the plan to mitigate drift, never for the agreements as attachments. |
| `g6_0_production.uses_production_equipment` | Whether any equipment contacts organic crops (CCOF G6.0 C1, WSDA I 1). OTCO C9 9.1-1 asks only about equipment shared with non-organic crops, which `equipment_shared_with_nonorganic` answers. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.carrier_handles_beyond_transport` | Whether a carrier packs, sorts, opens or labels the load. OTCO asks about shared transport equipment in C9 §9.1, not what the carrier does. |

| `g6_1_harvest_transport.container_cleaning_sop_upload` | The container cleaning procedure file. OTCO's C7 asks about the on-farm facility, packaging material and storage, not about harvest containers. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.container_types` | Which containers or bins hold the product at harvest (field bins, totes, buckets, bulk trailers, lugs, single-use cartons). C7 §7.9 asks a different axis — the packaging MATERIAL in direct contact with the product (flexible plastic, glass, metal, paper, hard plastic, compostable, cardboard, twine), recorded at 7.9-1 as not covered. Citing the form-factor list there would answer a question OTCO did not ask; it is listed as the trigger instead. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.container_types_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `container_types`; same axis difference as its parent. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.custom_harvester_cleanout_verified` | Whether the custom harvester's equipment cleanout is verified before it enters organic fields. | `parcel_application.landowner_phone` | WSDA AGR 2264 ref 7a/7b ask, for a site the operation does not own, the land owner's name, email, phone and address, and the lease details and who manages day to day. Not asked by OTCO. |

### WSDA

| Question | Why it has no WSDA counterpart |
|---|---|
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_areas` | Which risk areas describe the operation — split production, uncertified suppliers, supplier churn, complex chains, custom operators, seasonal labour, imports. §P never asks the operation to characterise its own vulnerability. It goes straight to controls, and its one risk-adjacent option, `vulnerability_assessment`, appears inside Trazo's mitigation list rather than WSDA's. The nearest WSDA question, §P 5, asks how SUPPLIERS are evaluated and approved, which is one risk area treated as a procedure. CCOF asks the risk-area checklist at G8.0 D1. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_risk_areas`; unmapped with its parent. §P has no risk-area list to carry an `other`. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_review_frequency` | When the plan itself is reviewed and updated — annually, on change, before inspection. §P asks how the plan is IMPLEMENTED (ref 2) and whether internal audits happen (ref 3), and WSDA runs a LIVING plan: a renewing operation updates the sections that changed rather than re-filing, so the form has no reason to ask for a review cadence the way an annual re-filing would. It is `triggered_by` on §P 3, where it indicates the section applies, but it does not answer it. CCOF asks the cadence directly on the Certification Contract, ref B2. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_review_frequency_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `osp_review_frequency`; unmapped with its parent. |
| `g3_0_seeds.buyer_search_documents` | The buyer's own search on contract-supplied seed. OTCO C3 3.3-3 asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 A1 asks the source only. |
| `g3_0_seeds.farm_grown_processing_contracted` | Contracted processing of farm-grown seed or transplants. OTCO C3 3.2-3 asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 A and B do not. |
| `g3_0_seeds.farm_grown_processing_description` | The detail of the contracted processing above; same reason. |
| `g3_0_seeds.grafting_practices` | Grafting practices. CCOF G3.0 E1a asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 C mentions grafting stock only within the commercial-availability search. |
| `g3_0_seeds.seed_treatment_types` | An inventory of treatment types. OTCO C3 3.5-1 asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 A2b and A3c ask yes or no and the materials list. |

Since 2026-11-05 the certificate each seedling supplier's purchase needs is the copy in the supplier register, which the G3.0a supplier panel (`seedling_suppliers_panel`) reads and the packet carries under suppliers/. A file uploaded here still rides in the packet under attachments/ and is listed on G3.0a; it answers no form item by itself. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.contract_stock_input_documentation` | Documentation that contracted stock used allowed inputs. OTCO C3 3.1-5a asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 C1 asks the source only. |

| `g3_2_planting_stock.nonorganic_stock_for_organic_crop` | Whether nonorganic stock grows a crop sold as organic. CCOF G3.0 A3a asks it; WSDA AGR 2121 C does not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_types_established` | Which propagation forms were established (bare-root, containerized, rootstock, cuttings/scions, crowns/divisions). WSDA's §C header DEFINES these forms — "any plant or plant tissue other than annual seedlings but including rhizomes, shoots, leaf or stem cuttings, roots, or tubers" — to set the section's scope, and then never asks which of them the operation uses. §C ref 1 asks acquisition SOURCE (nursery / own / contract / other), which is a different axis and is answered by `planting_stock_description` there. Citing this field against ref 1 would report propagation form as though it were source. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_initial_cn_ratio` | The initial carbon:nitrogen ratio of the feedstock, which § 205.203(c)(2) fixes between 25:1 and 40:1 as the precondition for the temperature window that follows. WSDA's §D 9a asks only for the OUTCOME and its evidence — how the pile is mixed and managed so all feedstocks reach 131°F (55°C) for at least three days, and what records demonstrate it — and never asks for the ratio that made that outcome achievable. §D 8 asks which feedstocks are used, by category (manure or other animal materials / plant materials / newspaper or other recycled paper / other), not in any proportion from which a ratio could be read. CCOF's G4.1 A2b does ask for the number. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_source` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (is the manure purchased or produced off-farm). WSDA §D asks whether raw manure is applied and how the interval and water-protection rules are met, never where the manure comes from. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_supplier_statement` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (label or supplier statement that purchased manure is untreated). WSDA's forms ask for no manure-provenance document; the material's listing is judged on AGR 2196 instead. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_supplier_statement_upload` | The label or supplier statement file itself. Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3; WSDA's forms ask for no manure-provenance document. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.conservation_plan_agency` | Whether a current conservation plan or agreement with an agency or programme exists (NRCS, RCD, a state programme). WSDA's §E asks which NRCS PRACTICES are used but never whether the operation is enrolled in a plan or programme with the agency those practices come from — the practice vocabulary is borrowed, the relationship is not asked about. CCOF asks it directly at G4.2 A2, where it is registered `covered`. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.conservation_plan_detail` | The agency or programme name and what its plan covers. Follow-on detail for `conservation_plan_agency` above; the same reasoning applies, and there is no §E question it could attach to. |

| `g4_2_natural_resources.monitoring_method_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `monitoring_method`; unmapped for the same reason as its parent. WSDA's nearest question, E8, is gated on "Do you apply input materials THROUGH YOUR IRRIGATION SYSTEM" — the operation's own chemigation. A district chlorinating or treating shared canal water triggers nothing in §E, because the operation applies nothing. CCOF asks the district case directly at G6.0 D3, which is a California-shaped question: shared surface-water districts are the normal delivery mechanism there. |

| `g4_2_natural_resources.wildlife_habitat_pressure` | Whether the operation removes or degrades wildlife habitat (land clearing, hedgerow removal), which is the trigger for the mitigation question that follows it. WSDA asks for biodiversity PRACTICES unconditionally at E2 and never establishes a pressure that would require offsetting; its only two conditional facts, E4 (permanent ground cover ≥ 90%) and E5 (slope < 10%), are erosion-risk skip logic, not habitat pressure. So the mitigation field has a home at E2 while its own trigger has none — CCOF asks the pair at A4 and A7. |
